title: Drop the fp32 logits upcast (bf16 softcap + cross-entropy)
description: Deleted one line in GPT.forward: 'logits = logits.float()', so the tanh softcap and F.cross_entropy run on bf16 logits; nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.981592 vs the 0.981817 baseline: -0.00023, a tie (0.3 sigma on the 8e-4 arm-to-arm floor). The predicted mechanism did not appear and the diagnostic is unambiguous: peak_vram_mb is 67804.2, IDENTICAL to the baseline's 67804.2, and tokens rose only 0.6% (308.0M / 1175 steps vs 306.2M / 1168). Inductor was already fusing the fp32 upcast into the tanh epilogue, so the 8.6GB fp32 logits tensor I costed out was never materialized -- my 20-33ms/step estimate was wrong at its root, not merely optimistic. I pre-registered 'tokens up <2% means the idea is dead whatever val_bpb says', so: dead. The residual positive result is that the epilogue's precision does not matter here -- bf16 log_softmax, a bf16 per-token loss into evaluate_bpb, and the coarser backward all cost nothing measurable, so the deletion is free and can be kept or dropped on style alone. Two generalisations for the remaining slots: (1) the memory-traffic region is closed, not just this instance -- if inductor already fused the largest pointwise chain in the model, hand-reasoning about HBM passes from the Python source will keep over-predicting; (2) peak_vram_mb is a cheap, reliable probe of what inductor actually materialized, and we should have read it off an existing run before spending a slot to learn it.
